sec: Portal hypertension pathophysiology and liver failure signs

items.q: Match each contributor to increased sinusoidal resistance in portal hypertension with its mechanism — 1) Mechanical cause 2) Functional cause … A) Decreased intrasinusoidal nitric oxide (NO) leading to vasoconstriction and defenestration B) Physical compression of sinusoidal channels by regenerating nodules
items.exp: The mechanical cause is compression by nodules; the functional cause is decreased intrasinusoidal NO causing sinusoidal vasoconstriction and defenestration. (Book p999)

items.q: What is the primary compensatory mechanism triggered by elevated portal venous pressure?
opts: Decompression via the formation of portosystemic collaterals
Selective spasm of the superior mesenteric artery
Upregulation of renal medullary aquaporin channels
items.exp: Increased portal venous pressure triggers the compensatory mechanism: 'Decompression, formation of collaterals'. (Book p999)

items.q: Assess the two statements on nitric oxide (NO) in cirrhosis: I Intrasinusoidal NO is decreased, driving sinusoidal vasoconstriction and defenestration. II Systemic NO is increased, inducing widespread splanchnic vasodilation and hyperdynamic circulation.
items.exp: Both statements are true: cirrhosis features decreased intrasinusoidal NO (increased intrahepatic resistance) alongside increased systemic NO (splanchnic vasodilation). (Book p999)

items.q: Fill up: In portal hypertension pathophysiology, gut endotoxemia and increased systemic nitric oxide cause a profound loss in peripheral vascular resistance, driving a ______ circulation that elevates portal inflow.
items.exp: The flowchart notes that loss in peripheral vascular resistance leads to 'Hyperdynamic circulation (↑ F)', where increased flow increases pressure. (Book p999)

items.q: How does splanchnic vasodilation stimulate neurohumoral volume retention in cirrhosis?
opts: Decreased effective circulatory volume triggers the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) and ADH
Direct mechanical stretching of atrial natriuretic peptide receptors
Suppression of central sympathetic adrenergic outflow
Excessive degradation of vasopressin by the damaged liver
items.exp: Widespread splanchnic vasodilation reduces effective circulatory volume, stimulating RAAS and ADH to expand intravascular volume and exacerbate the hyperdynamic state. (Book p999)

items.q: Match each early manifestation of elevated splenic vein pressure with its clinical milestone — 1) Splenomegaly (hypersplenism) 2) Thrombocytopenia … A) First biochemical finding (due to platelet trapping in the spleen) B) First clinical finding
items.exp: Elevated splenic vein pressure causes splenomegaly as the 'First clinical finding' and thrombocytopenia (due to platelet trapping) as the 'First biochemical finding'. (Book p999)

items.q: A 52-year-old man with compensated cirrhosis presents for routine follow-up. He has a palpably enlarged spleen. Complete blood count shows platelets 78,000/µL. What is the mechanism behind this initial biochemical abnormality?
opts: Trapping and pooling of platelets in the congested spleen secondary to raised splenic vein pressure
Autoimmune destruction of platelets by anti-platelet GPIIb/IIIa antibodies
Direct toxic suppression of megakaryocytes by ethanol metabolites
Accelerated consumption of platelets inside coronary atherosclerotic plaques
items.exp: Thrombocytopenia is the first biochemical finding, caused by the trapping of platelets within the congested spleen. (Book p999)

items.q: Which of the following physical signs of liver failure is attributed specifically to the hyperdynamic circulation rather than alcohol consumption?
items.exp: Palmar erythema and hyperpigmentation are features of the hyperdynamic circulation; alopecia, parotid swelling, and Dupuytren's contracture are associated with alcohol consumption. (Book p999)

items.q: Which triad of clinical signs is specifically grouped under 'Associated with Alcohol Consumption' on this page?
items.exp: The alcohol-associated features are explicitly listed as: Alopecia, Parotid Swelling, and Dupuytren's contracture. (Book p999)

items.q: Assess the two statements on cirrhosis hemodynamics: I Increased portal venous pressure is driven by both increased intrahepatic vascular resistance and increased portal blood flow. II Intrasinusoidal defenestration in cirrhosis is caused by an excess of intrasinusoidal nitric oxide.
items.exp: Statement I is true because P proportional to R x F. Statement II is false because defenestration and vasoconstriction are caused by decreased intrasinusoidal NO. (Book p999)
